messages:
marta: Heads up — seeing a spike in preemptions for the spot GPU pool in us-central1-b between 04:10–04:30 UTC. ~40% of recently launched spot nodes were reclaimed within ~3m. Pods with priority class `gpu-batch` got repeatedly evicted :warning:

infra-bot: [ALERT] spot-pool-us-central1-b: preemption_wave=high node_reclaims=37 window=20m — pushed notification to #incidents and pager duty

kai: Yikes. Any cloud maint notice? I don't see scheduled maint in console, looks like capacity churn. Did cluster-autoscaler fall back to on-demand nodegroup?

marta: CA attempted scale but many pods were unschedulable because the on-demand pool has `node.kubernetes.io/spot`-incompatible taints and our GPU daemonsets use `nodeSelector: spot: true`. So scheduler wouldn't place them.

sam: Quick suspicion: we rely on taint-based segregation for spot workloads; when spots vanish CA tries to create on-demand but pods are explicit about spot. We should either relax nodeSelector or add a spillover group that matches selectors.

kai: Agree. Two ideas: 1) Add a small on-demand fallback nodepool labelled `gpu-fallback=true` and ensure scheduler tolerations/affinity allow spillover. 2) Keep the spot-only label but add an autoscaler config for fallback that will be untainted (or have tolerations).

jen: Cost check: if we keep a 4-gpu on-demand buffer per region, monthly delta is roughly $12k/region (ballpark). But that buys availability. We should model the p99 cost impact for customer workloads before committing.

alex: If we do fallback nodes, we should ensure graceful eviction and KV cache priming. Also add an admission webhook to prefer spot nodes if available to reduce cold-starts.

sam: Proposed CA flags to test (canary):
```
--nodes=0:20:gpu-spot-us
--nodes=2:10:gpu-on-demand-fallback
--expander=least-waste
--max-node-provision-time=3m
--balance-similar-node-groups
```
We'll pin `gpu-on-demand-fallback` with label `gpu-fallback=true` and set a soft-taint `spot-spillover=true:PreferNoSchedule` so scheduler prefers spot but can place if needed.

kai: For pods, add a fallback toleration and softer affinity: `nodeSelector: spot: true` -> prefer via `preferredDuringSchedulingIgnoredDuringExecution` on label `spot=true`. That avoids code changes for most services.

marta: Operational playbook draft: 1) create fallback pool (2 nodes) in us-central1-canary, 2) update CA config, 3) update scheduler affinity rules via mutating webhook for gpu workloads, 4) run two 6h soak tests of batch and realtime inference, 5) monitor token latency and P95 cost.

jen: I'll run cost delta simulations and add to the PR. Sam — can you draft the CA changes?

sam: On it. I'll prepare a helm values patch and a small infra PR. Can we target a 48h canary starting tomorrow UTC 02:00?

alex: I'll add notes to the incident/runbook: check `kubectl get nodes -l gpu-fallback=true`, `kubectl describe node <node>` for taints, and look at `cluster-autoscaler` events. Also add a Grafana panel for fallback-pool-utilization.

marta: Thanks. Action owners: sam (CA PR), jen (cost model), alex (runbook + dashboards), kai (mutating webhook prototype). We'll reconvene after first 6h soak. :thumbsup:
